newsitem.title: IRAN: Ex-UN envoy, liberal critic to run in Iran poll.
newsitem.headline: Ex-UN envoy, liberal critic to run in Iran poll.

text.p: A former Iranian ambassador to the United Nations and a liberal opposition figure said they planned to run in Iran's presidential election in May.

Ezzatollah Sahabi, a liberal Islamist critic of government policies, told reporters on Monday he would register to run on a platform advocating easing tensions in Iran's foreign relations and guaranteeing freedom and security for Iranians at home.
Saeed Rajaei-Khorasani, a former U.N. envoy and parliament deputy, announced on Sunday he would stand as an an independent, the Iranian news agency IRNA said.

The announcements brought to eight the number of prospective candidates in the election to replace President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, who is barred by the constitution from running for a third consecutive four-year term.
Iran said on Sunday registration of candidates for the May 23 election would open on April 21.
Candidates will be screened by the Guardian Council, a body of lawyers and Shi'ite Moslem clerics which in past elections disqualified all but a handful of those who signed up.
Conservative Parliament Speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri appears to be the front-running candidate.

Hardline conservative Mohammad Mohammadi Reyshahari, a former internal security minister, and former minister of culture and Islamic guidance Mohammad Khatami, who is backed by radical Islamist intellectuals, are among others who have announced their candidacy.
Rafsanjani's centrist backers have yet to announce a candidate in the polls to replace the outgoing president, whose term ends on August 3.
